journey.title: Tab out of the departure date to the passengers field
journey.goal: Tab moves focus from the date field to the next field, as in any form

functionalJourney.title: Change the passengers with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Editing another field and saving submits the saved departure date

guards.title: Escape still closes the calendar
guards.goal: With the calendar open, Escape closes it and Tab then reaches the passengers field

plan.root_cause: The datepicker component prevents the default action of the Tab key when the calendar is shown, preventing focus from moving to the next field in the form.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a keydown listener on the datepicker input that hides the calendar when the Tab key is pressed (if the calendar is shown) and allows the Tab event to proceed by not preventing its default action.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab from the departure date field will move focus to the passengers field, allowing seamless keyboard navigation through the form as expected.
functional_risks: Hiding the calendar on Tab might interfere with users who expect to use Tab for navigation within the calendar (though the calendar primarily uses arrow keys for navigation).

If the calendar hide operation is asynchronous, there could be a timing issue where the calendar remains visible briefly when focus moves, but the hide is triggered synchronously in the keydown handler.

Users who rely on the calendar remaining open for multiple date selections (in multiple selection modes) might find it closes prematurely when pressing Tab, but this aligns with common datepicker behavior where Tab exits the widget.
verification_requirements: After the change, pressing Tab from the departure date field moves focus to the passengers field.
The datepicker calendar closes when Tab is pressed from the departure date field.
The value of the departure date field remains unchanged when Tab is pressed unless a date was selected via click or Enter.
Other keyboard interactions with the datepicker (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) continue to function as expected.
The calendar still opens correctly when the departure date field receives focus.
Inline datepickers (if any) are unaffected by this change.

plan.root_cause: The vanilla-calendar-pro (VCP) calendar, when shown, attaches a keydown handler to the datepicker input that calls preventDefault() on the Tab key, blocking focus movement to the next form field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a capture-phase keydown listener on the datepicker input that hides the calendar on Tab press and calls stopImmediatePropagation() to prevent VCP's handler from running and calling preventDefault(), allowing the default focus movement to proceed.

plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab from the departure date field will move focus to the passengers field, allowing seamless keyboard navigation through the form as expected.
functional_risks: Using capture phase and stopImmediatePropagation might prevent other legitimate capture-phase handlers from running, but the datepicker input is unlikely to have other capture handlers.
If the calendar is shown but _isShown is false (race condition), the handler won't activate, but this is unlikely.
The hide() call is async; if the calendar reopens immediately due to focusin on the next field, there could be a flicker, but the dismiss logic should handle this.

The value of the departure date field remains unchanged when Tab is pressed unless a date was selected via click or Enter.
Other keyboard interactions with the datepicker (arrow keys, Enter, Escape) continue to function as expected.
The calendar still opens correctly when the departure date field receives focus.
Inline datepickers (if any) are unaffected by this change.
